proposed_comments.title: Dispose the temporary SecureString after updating the local user
proposed_comments.body:
### Dispose the temporary SecureString after the local-user update

**Severity:** `medium`

**Affected code:** `.github/skills/ui-tests-local-vm/templates/oem/Set-UiTestAutoLogon.ps1`, the `$securePassword` update path around the `New-LocalUser` and `Set-LocalUser` calls.

**Problem:** The PR constructs a read-only `SecureString` but leaves it undisposed after either local-user cmdlet returns. The object can retain sensitive password material longer than necessary, including when a cmdlet throws.

**Why it matters:** This weakens the intended secret-lifetime improvement and makes cleanup depend on garbage collection rather than deterministic disposal on success and failure paths.

**Suggested change:**
1. Keep the character-by-character construction and `MakeReadOnly()` call.
2. Wrap the existing create-or-update block in `try`/`finally`.
3. Call `$securePassword.Dispose()` in `finally` so both branches release the temporary secure buffer even when the user update fails.

**Verification:** Parse the script with Windows PowerShell and exercise both the create-user and update-user branches, including a cmdlet failure, confirming the cmdlet receives the SecureString and cleanup always runs.
